sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cocidius was a god of northern Britain. The Romans joined him to their war god Mars, and the soldiers favoured him. Yet the horns he wore hint that he began as a god of hunters. That reading matches his other link to the god Silvanus. One inscription from Britain pairs Cocidius with Vernostonus, an obscure Celtic god, though the point of that bond stays hidden.
